title: The One-Sentence PM Template That Fixes Vague Problem Statements
description:
Most 'problem statements' in a PRD are just vague vibes dressed up as a document -- and vague statements produce scattered, mismatched solutions. Here's the four-part template (who, pain, situation, consequence, plus evidence) that makes two different engineers design roughly the same fix. Pulled from Module 3 of the Product Manager Mastery Path.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/03-problem-discovery/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Most 'problem statements' PMs write are just vague vibes dressed up as a doc. Here's the one-sentence template that fixes it.
Take this weak one: 'Users find onboarding confusing.' Sounds reasonable -- but two different engineers reading it would design two totally different fixes.
Now the strong version: new admins abandon setup at the permissions step, because the roles shown don't match their job titles -- and thirty percent of workspaces never invite a second user.

display.heading: Strong version
display.subheading: "...causing 30% of new workspaces to never invite a second user."

beats.narration: See the difference? It names the exact user, the trigger, the consequence, and the evidence behind it. That specificity is what makes two engineers build the same thing.

display.heading: Who + pain + situation + consequence
display.subheading: Plus evidence -- that's what makes it actionable
